newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Zaire's U.N. envoy now represents new regime.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's U.N. envoy now represents new regime.

text.p: The United Nations has been officially told that the charge d'affaires of Zaire's U.N. mission, appointed by the government of ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko, now represents the new regime of President Laurent Kabila, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Thursday.

He said Khabouji N'zaji Lukabu, who has headed the mission for the past six years in the absence of an ambassador, sent a letter informing Secretary-General Kofi Annan that Kabila was the new president.

The letter also said Kabila had changed the country's name to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, that there was a new national anthem and that the national flag would revert to the one raised in June 1960, on independence from Belgium.

Eckhard said the U.N. legal affairs office reviewed the letter and affirmed the validity of Lukabu's credentials, "and the secretary-general will therefore comply with its contents," including circulating it as an official document.
No other U.N. member had so far challenged the credentials of the mission, "which appears just to continue on, now representing the Democratic Republic of the Congo," he added.
Lukabu told Reuters that Zaire's U.N. mission closed its New York office in July 1994 as an economy measure, and had since operated from his home in suburban North Caldwell, N.J.

But its U.N. dues have been paid and he denied that he and the only other member of his staff had gone without any salary, though he said there had sometimes been delays in transferring money from Kinshasa. He denied that any other country had helped subsidise the mission.
